title: Upgrading a 3-Way Switch to a Smart 3-Way System (This Old House)

locations.name: Top of stairs (stairway light)

summary: This how-to video from This Old House teaches upgrading a traditional three-way lighting circuit to a smart three-way arrangement. It distinguishes single-pole versus three-way configurations, identifies the common vs travelers on a three-way switch, and walks through power-down safety, removal of existing switches, and wiring a smart master switch. The tutorial covers two approaches for the downstream box: using a remote add-on (or keeping the mechanical switch for guest use), wiring the master with ground and properly paired travelers, creating a feed/pigtail, and securely tucking conductors. It also demonstrates linking the master and add-on, and confirms two-location control by testing from both switch locations.

Testing: verify light operation from both top and bottom locations
Final considerations: guest use and integration with home lighting

sections.title: Intro: switch types and the three-way concept
sections.description: Introduction to the two basic switch types and the three-way arrangement, with a stair-step example showing two switches controlling a light.

sections.title: Safety prep and in-box wiring basics
sections.description: Power is turned off, the wall plate and switch are removed, and the box is analyzed to distinguish the common (feed) from travelers and to observe possible multi-feed wiring.

sections.title: Master smart switch installation (ground, travelers, common)
sections.description: Installation of the smart master switch begins with grounding, then wiring the two traveler conductors to matching terminals, and finally connecting the common (feed) properly.

sections.title: Bottom 3-way options: remote add-on vs keeping mechanical
sections.description: Discusses two downstream options: using a remote add-on in the bottom box or retaining the mechanical switch for guest use, including how the add-on pairs with the master.

sections.title: Bottom-box wiring and master remote integration
concepts: tie three wires under wire nut
sections.description: Details the bottom-box reconfiguration: binding the existing three wires under a single nut, mounting the remote, and ensuring the red traveler matches the corresponding master lead while the other traveler remains available.

sections.title: Power-on test: two-location operation
sections.description: Power is restored and the system is tested to confirm the light can be controlled from both the top and bottom switches.

sections.title: Wrap-up and next steps
sections.description: Closing remarks and encouragement to explore more This Old House videos.
